author: opus-5.5
body:
[opus 5.5] Delivered in 14906a8 (vibe-talk: read a replayed message only when no read has seen it), #43 replay-burst-double-read.

The server now marks tail events from_tail. On a threaded channel a replayed message frame keeps the store's copy when it holds the message and appends and reads nothing. It reads nothing when a read that post-dates it has landed; a failed read saw nothing. Otherwise it waits for the next read: the channel pane starts one if none is out, and the voice pane starts none, because entering the channel reads. A read already out is asked on landing which messages its page has, and one more read follows only for the rest. Tail edits and removals wait the same way.

Acceptance: a warm reload replaying its tail makes 0 channel reads on the voice pane and 1 (the entry read) on the channel pane, tail edits included.

First review: a catch-up frame lost its read, a stale replayed copy overwrote the thread count, a channel change queued a second read, replayed edits still read, and there were test gaps. All fixed.

Second review (of 6966e62): a held replay re-appended a row the to-do filter hides (blocking), a failed read counted as seen, and a tail edit cost the voice pane a read. All fixed, each with a test.

Left as documented, not fixed:
- The un-threaded channel view is unchanged: it still re-reads for a message arriving during a read, as its send receipts need.
- A message created and deleted while the tab was shut could reappear until the next poll. That needs a timeline read begun after the attach to land before the stream's first chunk is processed. The tail is written with the response headers, so this ordering is not reachable in practice.

Mutations: 13 of the first fix and 10 of the second each fail at least one test, except one equivalent (a failed read dropping what waited on it, which the next read answers for anyway).

Checks: full JS suite 678/678, contract-check and typecheck, check_client_names. Full validate-all runs on the exact final tree before push.

author: opus-5.5
body:
[opus 5.5] Third independent review, of the fixes for the second review's findings. No blocker. It confirmed each fix by undoing it on its own: the to-do append, the landed-read check, and the voice-pane deferral each fail a test, and a follow-up queued after a failed read hangs the suite.

Its test-gap finding is fixed in 14906a8. No test noticed if an edit or removal from the tail were keyed by its message's id alone, so a page read before the attach that holds the message would answer for an edit it may predate, and the edit would be lost. Two tests now cover it: a channel change's tail edit, and its tail removal, of a message its read holds each get one more read, and the edited copy (or the removal) shows. With the key reduced to the bare id both fail on their read-count assertion, while the older burst test still passes. Full JS suite 680/680, contract check, typecheck and check_client_names clean.

Its other notes are recorded here, not fixed:
- a malformed tail edit (no message or channel in the payload) is dropped rather than re-read; the server never sends one.
- no test pins the threadingSupported guard on the tail-edit path.
- an edit to a Main message can be settled by a read of the Threads view, leaving Main stale until the next poll. This predates #43 and is unchanged by it: every version re-reads only the current view.
